analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB read occurs because NFLOG TLV validation is too weak before dereferencing TLV header fields. NflogTlv::canAssign() only requires 2 bytes (recordLen) but getTotalSize() reads m_Data->recordLen from a candidate next-record pointer that may have fewer than 2 valid bytes remaining. TLVData::TLVRecordReader::getNextTLVRecord() calls resRec.getTotalSize() immediately after assign(), so malformed/truncated TLV streams can force a read past the end. Crash manifests at NflogLayer.h:109 during NflogLayer::parseNextLayer()->getTlvByType()->getTLVRecord()->getNextTLVRecord().
analyzed_vuln.conditions: FuzzTarget feeds a crafted .pcap/.pcapng packet that is parsed as NFLOG. Packet data length is enough to pass NflogLayer::isDataValid (>= nflog_header), but TLV area is malformed/truncated such that iteration reaches a next TLV pointer near end-of-buffer. Because canAssign accepts only 2-byte minimum and pointer arithmetic in getNextTLVRecord permits this candidate, getTotalSize() dereferences recordLen out of bounds, triggering ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.
